deadline_label: Submit ≥ 3–4 months before start date; Migrationsverket processing 1–4 months

field_label: Mandatory Union Consultation Before Work Permit Submission
deadline_label: Obtain before submitting permit application; allow 2–3 weeks for union response
non_obvious_official_guidance: Swedish immigration law requires the employer to consult the relevant trade union (facklig organisation) and obtain a written statement (fackligt yttrande) confirming that the employee's salary and working conditions meet applicable collective bargaining agreement (kollektivavtal) standards before submitting a work permit application to Migrationsverket.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Most non-Nordic HR generalists have never heard of this requirement. Even if the employee is not a union member, the employer must identify and contact the relevant industry union. Missing this step causes automatic rejection of the permit application by Migrationsverket — there is no cure or fast-track after the fact. Union processing times vary; some take 1 week, others 3–4 weeks. The union may also flag salary below market rate, delaying or blocking the permit.
non_obvious_action_required: Before drafting the employment contract, identify the relevant Swedish trade union for the employee's role and industry (e.g. Unionen for white-collar, IF Metall for manufacturing, Akademikerförbunden for professionals). Contact the union's employer services (arbetsgivarsida) section, provide the draft contract and salary terms, and obtain a signed fackligt yttrande. Submit this document with the permit application package on the Migrationsverket employer portal.
source: Migrationsverket — Employer responsibilities when applying for a work permit

field_label: Register Posted Worker with Arbetsmiljöverket Before Assignment
deadline_label: Must notify before first working day in Sweden
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under the Posted Workers Directive (EU 2018/957), transposed into Swedish law via the Utstationeringslagen, employers posting workers to Sweden must register the posting in the Utstationeringssystemet (posting notification system) run by Arbetsmiljöverket and designate a contact/liaison person physically present or reachable in Sweden before the assignment begins.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This registration is routinely missed by HR generalists unfamiliar with Swedish labour law. Sweden actively enforces posted worker rules; Arbetsmiljöverket conducts inspections and can issue fines for unregistered postings. Beyond regulatory risk, failure to register undermines the social security coordination argument: an A1 certificate is harder to defend if the posting itself was never formally notified. Additionally, the employer may be jointly liable for sub-contractors' posted worker violations.
non_obvious_action_required: Register via Arbetsmiljöverket's online portal before the employee's first Swedish working day. Designate a liaison person (can be a local HR contact or external legal representative). Keep the home-country A1 certificate (see ONGOING step) on file with both the liaison and the employee. Note: the liaison person must be reachable throughout the posting — a UK or Paris-based HR generalist does not satisfy this requirement.
source: Arbetsmiljöverket — Posting of workers to Sweden

form_name: No formal permit — right of residence (uppehållsrätt) applies automatically
field_label: EU/EEA Nationals: Right of Residence — No Work Permit Required
deadline_label: Right applies from day 1 of employment; no registration required for stays under 3 months

field_label: Register Place of Residence for Personnummer (Folkbokföring)
deadline_label: Register within first week of arrival; personnummer issued 1–4 weeks after registration
non_obvious_official_guidance: Folkbokföring is the Swedish population registration system. To register, the employee must appear in person at a Skatteverket service centre with original documents (passport, work permit card or EU/EEA identity document, and proof of a fixed Swedish address) and demonstrate an intended stay of at least one year.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 'at least one year' residency intent requirement is a hard eligibility gate that many HR generalists overlook. Employees on short-term contracts of under 12 months cannot register for folkbokföring and will not receive a personnummer — they need a samordningsnummer instead (see step 8). Additionally, a confirmed Swedish address (signed lease) is required at the point of registration: hotel stays and temporary serviced apartments typically do not qualify. Walk-in availability at Skatteverket offices in Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö is severely limited — appointment booking is essential.
non_obvious_action_required: Before arrival, confirm that the employment contract clearly states a start date implying ≥ 12 months of intended Swedish residency. Secure a permanent lease agreement (not hotel) before booking the Skatteverket registration appointment. Book the appointment in advance via Skatteverket's online booking system — same-week walk-in slots are rare in major cities. Without folkbokföring, there is no personnummer, which blocks BankID, bank accounts, and most digital Swedish services.
source: Skatteverket — Moving to Sweden and registering

authority: Private rental market (Blocket Bostad, Qasa) / Hyresgästföreningen
field_label: Secure Permanent Housing with Formal Lease
deadline_label: Required before folkbokföring registration; arrange before or immediately upon arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: Folkbokföring registration requires a registered permanent Swedish address. Without a signed lease, the employee cannot register with Skatteverket, which in turn blocks personnummer issuance.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Stockholm and Gothenburg have among the most constrained rental markets in Europe. The municipal housing queue (Bostadsförmedlingen) has waiting times of 10–20 years. New arrivals depend almost entirely on the private rental market. Many private landlords in Sweden require proof of Swedish income, a personnummer, and local references — creating a circular dependency at arrival: no housing → no personnummer → no BankID → no digital lease agreement. Without employer intervention, this can take 6–8 weeks to resolve.
non_obvious_action_required: Arrange employer-sponsored temporary accommodation (corporate apartment, Bloxster, or serviced stay with a formal address) covering at least the first 4–8 weeks. Ensure the temporary accommodation address can be used for folkbokföring (confirm with the provider). Engage a Swedish relocation agent if budget allows — they have standing relationships with private landlords who accept new arrivals without personnummer. An employer letter confirming salary and contract length can substitute for personnummer with some landlords.

field_label: Personnummer (Personal Identity Number) — Receipt and Downstream Unblocking
deadline_label: Issued 1–4 weeks after folkbokföring; follow up at 3 weeks if not received
non_obvious_official_guidance: The personnummer (format YYYYMMDD-XXXX) is issued automatically by Skatteverket following successful folkbokföring registration. It is the primary identifier for all Swedish public and private services.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The personnummer is the master gating credential for life in Sweden. Without it: no BankID (digital identity), no Swedish bank account at most banks, no access to Mina Sidor at Skatteverket, no 1177.se healthcare portal, no Försäkringskassan online account. The downstream chain — personnummer → bank account → BankID — takes a minimum of 4–8 weeks from arrival. Processing can run to 8+ weeks during high-volume periods (January and post-summer). Employees routinely arrive expecting digital access within days; the reality is weeks of functional exclusion from Swedish digital infrastructure.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief employees pre-departure: expect a 4–8 week window with no Swedish digital access. Provide a corporate credit/debit card, cash advance, and employer-issued mobile phone with a Swedish SIM. Chase Skatteverket proactively if the personnummer has not arrived after 3 weeks — delays can compound into banking and BankID delays of 2–3 additional weeks.

field_label: Coordination Number (Samordningsnummer) — For Employees Ineligible for Personnummer
deadline_label: Apply as soon as possible; employer submits on employee's behalf via Skatteverket
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees who cannot register for folkbokföring (intended stay under 12 months) can obtain a samordningsnummer through a Swedish authority that has cause to identify them — most commonly via the employer submitting form SKV 7002 to Skatteverket to enable correct income tax withholding.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A samordningsnummer is NOT functionally equivalent to a personnummer. It does not grant access to BankID; most major Swedish banks will not open accounts with it; it does not activate Försäkringskassan digital services or the 1177 healthcare portal. It serves primarily as a tax identifier for payroll purposes. Short-term assignees using a samordningsnummer effectively have no Swedish digital identity for the duration of their assignment and must manage all financial and administrative matters via foreign accounts, employer intermediaries, or physical visits to offices.
non_obvious_action_required: Identify before departure whether the employee's contract qualifies for folkbokföring (≥12 months) or samordningsnummer (<12 months). If samordningsnummer is required, have the employer submit SKV 7002 to Skatteverket promptly. Contact the employee's bank in their home country to confirm their foreign card will work in Sweden for daily expenses throughout the assignment. Do not assume the employee will be able to open a Swedish bank account.

form_name: Mina Sidor account activation — Försäkringskassan portal
deadline_label: Activate as soon as personnummer is received; employer reports employee via monthly AGI payroll filing

form_name: Bank Account Application — varies by bank
deadline_label: Open after personnummer received; allow 4–6 weeks from arrival for full account access
source: Konsumenternas — Choosing a bank in Sweden

form_name: BankID Application (via issuing bank's branch or app)
deadline_label: Apply via bank after bank account is active; typically 1–2 weeks after account opening
non_obvious_official_guidance: BankID is a private digital identity service issued by Swedish banks, used by virtually all Swedish government agencies, banks, healthcare portals, and private services for authentication and legally binding digital signing.
non_obvious_actual_reality: BankID can only be obtained after a bank account is open, which requires a personnummer first. The chain is strictly sequential: personnummer → bank account → BankID. There is no shortcut. Without BankID, the employee cannot authenticate to Mina Sidor (Skatteverket), 1177.se (healthcare), Försäkringskassan digital services, digital lease signing, or most Swedish employer HR self-service portals. The full chain from arrival to active BankID takes 4–8 weeks under normal conditions.
non_obvious_action_required: Communicate the 4–8 week timeline to the employee well before departure. Identify which bank offers the fastest onboarding for new residents — Handelsbanken and SEB have dedicated new-resident pathways in Stockholm and Gothenburg. Consider providing the employee a corporate Mastercard/Visa for the interim. Note: Mobilt BankID (mobile app) is issued separately from BankID on file — ensure the employee activates the mobile version, as most services now require the mobile version.

form_name: Application for Swedish National ID Card (Nationellt identitetskort)
field_label: Swedish Residence Permit Card / National ID Card
deadline_label: Residence permit card issued with initial work permit grant; national ID card available post-personnummer at police office

form_name: A-skatt / Skattetabell (Tax Table) — Employer withholding setup
field_label: Swedish Income Tax — A-skatt Employer Preliminary Withholding
deadline_label: Employer must apply correct tax table from first salary payment
source: Skatteverket — Tax for employees working in Sweden

field_label: SINK — Special Income Tax for Non-Residents (25% flat rate)
deadline_label: Submit before first salary payment; retroactive correction is generally not available
non_obvious_official_guidance: SINK (Särskild inkomstskatt för utomlands bosatta) is a flat 25% withholding tax available to employees who are not tax-resident in Sweden (i.e. not folkbokförd) and who meet eligibility criteria. Application is via form SKV 4350 and must be approved by Skatteverket before payroll runs.
non_obvious_actual_reality: SINK is frequently the more favorable option for short-term assignees, especially those earning above approximately SEK 600,000/year (above which Swedish progressive tax exceeds 25%). However, many employers default to progressive A-skatt without checking SINK eligibility, and this default cannot be corrected retroactively for payments already processed. SINK also differs structurally: no Swedish deductions (ROT/RUT, pension, commuting) can be claimed, so it is unfavorable for employees who would benefit from those deductions. The decision must be made proactively — once A-skatt has been withheld, the employee must file a Swedish tax return to claim any overpayment.
non_obvious_action_required: For every employee not folkbokförd in Sweden (short-term contract, under 183 days per calendar year), assess SINK eligibility before the first payroll run. Submit SKV 4350 to Skatteverket and wait for the approval decision — this can take 2–4 weeks. Coordinate with the employee's home-country tax advisor to confirm SINK is consistent with their tax treaty position and will not trigger unexpected home-country liabilities. For employees on a Swedish double-tax treaty, verify treaty relief is correctly applied under SINK.
source: Skatteverket — Special income tax for non-residents (SINK)

field_label: Annual Swedish Tax Return — Filed by 2 May Each Year
deadline_label: 2 May each year (extension to 15 May available); Skatteverket pre-populates a draft declaration
source: Skatteverket — Filing your income tax return

authority: Home-country social security authority (e.g. URSSAF/CPAM for France, NAV for Norway) / Försäkringskassan
form_name: A1 Certificate (Intyg A1 — Certificate of Coverage)
field_label: Social Security Totalization — A1 Certificate Prevents Double Contributions
deadline_label: Obtain before first Swedish working day; valid for initial posting period up to 24 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under EU Regulation 883/2004, an employee posted from one EU/EEA country to Sweden remains covered by their home country's social security system during the posting, provided the employer obtains an A1 certificate from the home-country social security authority before the assignment begins. This prevents Swedish social contributions from applying.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without a valid A1 certificate in place from day one, Sweden may claim social security contributions from both the employer and employee under Swedish law, creating costly double contributions that are extremely difficult to recover retroactively. Försäkringskassan actively checks A1 status during workplace inspections and audits — particularly in construction, logistics, and professional services. The A1 must be obtained before the first working day, not applied for after the fact. Complex situations — such as the employee splitting time between Sweden and their home country — require an explicit ruling from Försäkringskassan on which country's scheme applies; home-country A1 alone is insufficient in multi-country work patterns.
non_obvious_action_required: Initiate the A1 certificate request with the home-country social security authority (e.g. URSSAF in France, NAV in Norway, DVFA/Udbetaling Danmark in Denmark) before the posting contract is signed. Confirm A1 receipt and validity dates with Försäkringskassan if the employee will also work remotely from the home country during the posting. If the posting exceeds 24 months, apply for an extension or determine whether Swedish social security should apply for the remainder. File the A1 certificate with the Swedish liaison person (see PRE_DEPARTURE step 3) and keep a copy accessible during any Arbetsmiljöverket inspection.
source: Försäkringskassan — A1 certificate for workers posted to Sweden
